Foundations

A mathematical neuron

An early mathematical account of how networks of idealized neurons could carry out logical operations.

Warren S. McCulloch and Walter Pitts

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

Neural networksComputation theoryLogic

The contribution

McCulloch and Pitts modeled nervous activity with simplified, all-or-none units and logical relations. The paper connected the organization of a network to the computations it could represent, helping establish a formal language for studying neural computation.

What this does not establish

These were idealized units, not a full biological model. The paper did not introduce the learned weights or training procedures used in modern neural networks.

Why this date?

1943 is the publication year of the linked journal article.
